geometry_edits.rationale: Preserve the dominant mass as a courtyard-based primary body, but make the void logic the central rule.
Tune the carved void to read as a substantial public court without over-fragmenting the volume.
Open the court toward the access side so the mass responds coherently to the primary frontage.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the dominant carved-bar logic, but make the courtyard more explicit and legible as the primary spatial figure.
Slightly reduce carving depth so the primary mass remains a strong anchor while preserving a readable void.
Align the public opening with the verified access side to strengthen the street threshold.
Retarget the secondary void so the projection reinforces the same frontage-oriented public reading instead of competing with it.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact mass across the four views, but the gesture is still only moderately coherent: the top and oblique views suggest a carved courtyard/bar, while the front and opposite views drift toward a blunt truncated block. The parcel is respected overall, yet the mass largely fills the envelope instead of clearly organizing a dominant street-building figure relative to the thin green boundary. The thick blue frontage is acknowledged only weakly: there is some undercut/void logic, but the access edge does not become a legible public threshold with clear orientation. Program-wise, neighborhood living can support this kind of compact carved bar, but the current roof/section and massing hierarchy do not strongly express active-ground/public-void/upper-calm relationships. It is coherent enough to be salvageable, but not a hard pass because the public edge and sectional logic are underdeveloped and the form sits between object and court without fully committing to either.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion/cultural in tone than compact neighborhood living; avoid copying the sculptural roof silhouette.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a large central void and a bridge-like upper connection can support a civic neighborhood threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more dispersed than the candidate; do not imitate the tower-podium field condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like low-rise composition uses courtyards and stepped blocks to create shared public space at neighborhood scale.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Leans more retail/hospitality and greenhouse-like than the candidate’s compact block; facade transparency is not the point.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long horizontal massing with a carved central void and a responsive roof can make an active mixed-use ground figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more landscape-integrated and horizontally extended; candidate currently lacks that sectional continuity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced ribbon-like section and connected wings can produce a coherent public promenade and sectional hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More complex and multi-wing than the candidate; useful as a void/hierarchy precedent, not as an object to copy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes around a courtyard, with upper bridging and undercut ground, give a strong public threshold.

warnings: Open-space logic is present but not yet clearly public or front-loaded toward the verified access edge.
The silhouette changes meaning across views, so the dominant gesture is not fully stable in section and elevation.
The form risks reading as a generic block with a cut rather than a deliberate neighborhood threshold building.
